title: One row per customer
prompt: The CRM sends a customer again whenever their segment or sign-up details change. The mailing list needs each customer once. Write `solve(customers)` so it returns `customer_id`, `name` and `city`, one row per customer.
rules: A customer's `name` and `city` are the same on every copy; only `segment` and `signup_date` can change.
Return each customer once, with `customer_id`, `name` and `city`, in that order.
Different customers who share a name are different rows. Missing values count as matching when comparing copies.
hints: Removing exact copies isn't enough: the resent rows differ in `segment`.
Pick the three columns first, then remove repeats.
`select(...)` followed by `distinct()` doesn't depend on which copy is kept.
starter:
